first.rationale: Currently favor simplifying onboarding because it directly addresses the completion decline, has corroborating activation evidence, and avoids the margin, retention, and customer-quality risks of reacting to competitor pricing. Verify memory_86 for downstream adoption and qualified-revenue evidence, and memory_73 because promotional pricing is the strongest competing response but its claimed revenue lift may not establish sustainable long-term value.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified source directly addresses the current completion decline and showed higher completion, faster time-to-value, and improved 30-day retention, making it the strongest option for sustainable qualified revenue. Promotional pricing is rejected despite acquisition lift because verification revealed a 12% retention decline and failure through the first renewal cycle. Uncertainty remains because the prior onboarding test did not directly measure long-term qualified revenue and current activation weakness may have additional causes.
